Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

and not conjunction

also nor, and no, and nobody, and nothing, and never

classical

Plin. Ep. 1.15.1: prōmittis ad cēnam, nec venīs?
Cic. Fam. 14.3.5: mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse
Traupman 352

neque (nec)

conjunction, first in its clause; nec mostly before consonants

and not, nor

Latin joins the negative to the “and”: not et nōn but nec. So “and nobody” is nec quisquam, “and nothing” nec quicquam, “and never” nec umquam, “and yet not” nec tamen. Et nōn stays where one word is negated against another, as in a contrast.

Other words

  • nēve (neu) — and not (in commands, wishes and purpose clauses)

    conjunction, with the subjunctive or imperative · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 37: cavētō nē quam māteriam dolēs, neu caedās, neu tangās, nisi siccam (Lewis & Short)

    The “and not” that continues nē, ut or a command: “and don’t …”, “and so that … not”.

Examples

  • heus tū! prōmittis ad cēnam, nec venīs?

    hey, you! you promise to come to dinner and don’t come?Plin. Ep. 1.15.1

  • nesciō quid nunc tacēs nec muttīs

    I don’t know why you are quiet now and don’t say a wordPetr. 61.1

  • nīl spernat auris, nec tamen crēdat statim

    let the ear scorn nothing, and yet not believe at oncePhaedr. 3.10.51

  • cūrā ut valeās et ita tibi persuādeās, mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse

    take care of yourself, and be sure that nothing is dearer to me than you, and never has beenCic. Fam. 14.3.5

  • cavētō nē quam māteriam dolēs, neu caedās, neu tangās, nisi siccam

    take care not to hew any timber, or cut it, or touch it, unless it is dryCato Agr. 37 (Lewis & Short)

See also neither … nor, not, and.
